title: Your Stop
recap: You're trapped on a train you can't get off, and something is calling you in your mom's voice.
summary: June ends the call: rule five, it isn't them. She shows her lace-punched ticket: her stop was November 3, 1987, her mother waited on the platform smiling too wide, and she stayed on, and has stayed on ever since. But rule six says get off at your stop no matter what is on the platform, and the rules are in your own handwriting. Your reflection keeps reading after you look up, then blinks; you look away (rule eight). The route map scrambles into your name, the train stops, and your mom is on the platform, smiling too wide. June begs you to stay; the rules say go. The lamp flickers and she is one step closer.

lines.spoken: It's still talking. "Get off at the next stop, honey. I'm right here."
lines.caption: **I'm right here**

lines.spoken: June pulls the phone from your ear and ends the call.
lines.caption: June **ends the call**

lines.spoken: "Rule five," she says. "If someone calls your name, it isn't them."
lines.caption: **it isn't them**

lines.spoken: Your hands won't stop shaking. "It sounded exactly like her."
lines.caption: **exactly like her**

lines.spoken: "They always do." June picks her knitting back up, but her needles keep missing.
lines.caption: **they always do**

lines.spoken: "How do you know all this?" you ask.
lines.caption: **how do you know**

lines.spoken: June is quiet for a long time. Then she holds up her ticket, punched so many times it looks like lace.
lines.caption: **like lace**

lines.spoken: "November third, nineteen eighty seven. That was my stop."
lines.caption: **my stop**

lines.spoken: "My mother was waiting on the platform, waving. Smiling too wide."
lines.caption: **smiling too wide**

lines.spoken: "So I stayed on." She looks down at her ticket. "I've stayed on ever since."
lines.caption: **ever since**

lines.spoken: You unfold the rules sheet again.
lines.caption: the **rules** sheet

lines.spoken: Rule six. Your stop is the one that shows your name on the map. Get off, no matter what is on the platform.
lines.caption: **get off**, no matter what

lines.spoken: "June, the rules say you should have gotten off."
lines.caption: you should have **gotten off**

lines.spoken: Her needles stop. She doesn't look at you.
lines.caption: her needles **stop**

lines.spoken: Then you notice the handwriting.
lines.caption: the **handwriting**

lines.spoken: The loops on the g's. The little line through the sevens.
lines.caption: the **sevens**

lines.spoken: It's your handwriting. Yours.
lines.caption: **your** handwriting. **yours**

lines.spoken: "I didn't write this," you whisper. "I've never seen this before."
lines.caption: **I didn't write this**

lines.spoken: In the black window, your reflection is still looking down at the page.
lines.caption: your **reflection**

lines.spoken: You're already looking up. It isn't.
lines.caption: **it isn't**

lines.spoken: Then your reflection lifts its head. And blinks.
lines.caption: **blinks**

lines.spoken: You look away so fast your neck cracks.
lines.caption: **look away**

lines.spoken: "Rule eight," June whispers. "Good. Don't look back at it."
lines.caption: **don't look back**

lines.spoken: Above the doors, the route map flickers.
lines.caption: the **route map**

lines.spoken: The name of the next stop scrambles, letter by letter.
lines.caption: **letter by letter**

lines.spoken: Then it spells your name.
lines.caption: **your name**

lines.spoken: The brakes start to squeal. The train is slowing down.
lines.caption: **slowing down**

lines.spoken: June grabs your wrist. "Don't get off. Look at what's waiting."
lines.caption: **don't get off**

lines.spoken: The doors chime and slide open.
lines.caption: the doors **open**

lines.spoken: It's your mom, standing on the platform in her work coat, waving.
lines.caption: **your mom**

lines.spoken: She is smiling. Too wide.
lines.caption: **too wide**

lines.spoken: June's grip tightens. "It isn't her, sweetheart. It never is."
lines.caption: **it never is**

lines.spoken: But the rules, in your handwriting, say get off, no matter what is on the platform.
lines.caption: **no matter what**

lines.spoken: Behind your mom, the platform lamp flickers off.
lines.caption: the lamp **flickers off**

lines.spoken: When it comes back on, she's one step closer to the doors.
lines.caption: **one step closer**

continuity_out: Night 1, about 2:20 AM. The train is stopped at your stop (the route map shows your name), doors open. Your mom (or the thing wearing her) is on the platform, one step closer each time the lamp flickers. June holds your wrist and begs you to stay; she stayed on at her own stop in 1987 and has ridden ever since (her ticket is punched like lace). Rule six says get off no matter what is on the platform. The rules are in your own handwriting and you don't remember writing them. Your reflection blinked before you; you looked away. Your ticket has one hole.
